rejected_videos.reason: No clean standalone range adequately covers the required facts within this path's prerequisites. Preparation (63–143) explains goals, agendas, questions, and capture materials, but does not explain choosing activities to answer questions or allocating time to workshop segments. The worked agenda (146–233) depends on the earlier process-model case study and its untaught process notation. Execution (235–324) demonstrates goal-directed moderation but does not cover analyzing and sharing outputs after the workshop. Extending into the template introduces blocked acceptance criteria at 373; the follow-up introduces blocked requirements verification and validation at 480 before explaining distribution at 504. Trimming these sections would leave the claimed facts incomplete.

Reject for materially inaccurate methodological claims, not merely missing coverage. At 631–638 the speaker claims nobody can remember anything occurring more than two weeks earlier; at 829–844 she claims users asked about their work will never report anything true; and at 1473–1484 and 1513–1545 she claims interpretation of real-life activity cannot influence participants and dismisses concerns about bias. These absolutes are misleading. The instructions to never ask what users usually do (676–687) also conflict with this path's required stated-process recording and stated-versus-observed comparison (f4). Although the context and partnership sections contain useful explanations of observing actual work and asking about observed actions, trimming those sections would not resolve the video-level accuracy concerns. No clean segment teaches the required discrepancy-recording practice.
